title: 부모님 공원 산책 효과, 집에서 15분 거리면 될까요
description: 공원 산책 효과가 궁금한 자녀를 위한 글입니다. 24,341명 연구에서 집에서 15분 안에 공원이 있는 사람들은 우울 증상 비율이 6% 낮았어요.
image_alt: 공원 산책 효과를 떠올리게 하는, 공원 벤치에서 책을 읽는 할아버지와 떨어지는 낙엽을 그린 수채화
image_prompt: Watercolor illustration of an elderly man reading a book on a park bench with falling autumn leaves.
body_markdown:
「오늘은 어디 좀 다녀오셨어요?」 하고 여쭈면 부모님은 「그냥 집에 있었지」 하고 답하십니다. 크게 아픈 데는 없다는데 말수가 줄고 목소리가 가라앉은 것 같아, 전화를 끊고도 마음이 쓰입니다. 그럴 때 문득 부모님 댁 앞 공원이 떠오르지요. 공원 산책 효과라는 말, 어디까지 믿어도 될까요.

답부터 말씀드리면, 거창한 명소보다 집에서 가까운 공원이 먼저입니다. 남아프리카공화국 성인 24,341명을 조사한 연구에서, 가장 가까운 공원이 걸어서 15분 안에 있다고 답한 사람들은 15분보다 멀다고 답한 사람들보다 우울 증상을 가진 비율이 6% 낮았습니다(유병비 0.94)[5]. 조사 연구라서 원인이라고 단정할 수는 없지만, 눈여겨볼 만한 결과예요.

## 공원 산책 효과는 정말 있을까요?

여러 연구에서 녹지와 마음 건강 사이에 좋은 관련이 나타났지만, 연구마다 대상이 달라 그대로 옮기기는 조심스럽습니다. 14~24세를 다룬 연구 48편을 모은 고찰에서는, 실험 연구들이 녹지를 걷거나 그곳에 머문 직후 기분과 불안이 나아졌다고 보고했어요[1]. 다만 이 고찰은 젊은 사람들을 본 것이어서 어르신도 똑같다고 말할 수는 없습니다.

왜 그럴까에 대한 설명도 흥미롭습니다. 연구자들은 소음이 없고 마음이 쉬어 가는 공간의 성질이, 같은 걱정을 자꾸 곱씹는 일을 끊어 줄 수 있다는 틀을 내놓았어요[1]. 혼자 집에 계시면 걱정이 되풀이되기 쉽다는 것을 떠올리면 고개가 끄덕여지는 이야기입니다. 아직은 설명의 틀이지, 증명이 끝난 결론은 아니에요.

## 공원은 집에서 얼마나 가까워야 할까요?

앞서 본 남아프리카공화국 연구에서 나눈 기준은 걸어서 15분이었습니다[5]. 이 시간은 사람들이 스스로 답한 것이고, 연구는 18세 이상 전체를 본 것이라 35~59세에서 관련이 더 뚜렷했어요[5]. 어르신만의 숫자는 아니라는 점을 기억해 주세요.

그래도 영국 연구가 같은 방향을 가리킵니다. 잉글랜드 주민 21,097명의 자료에서 바닷가 가까이 사는 사람일수록 전반적인 건강과 마음 건강이 좋다고 답했고, 이 관련의 일부는 주로 걷기인 야외 활동으로 설명되었어요[4]. 좋은 곳에 산다는 사실만이 아니라, 그곳을 실제로 걷는 일이 함께 작용한다는 뜻입니다. 걷기는 운동이기 전에 세상과 다시 이어지는 문이고, 그 문은 가까울수록 자주 열립니다.

## 공원에는 얼마나 오래 머물면 좋을까요?

몇 분이 정답이라고 말할 수는 없지만, 머무는 시간이 길수록 건강 지표가 좋은 쪽으로 나타난 연구가 있습니다. 중국 선전에서 고혈압이 있는 35세 이상 1116명을 조사했더니, 공원 같은 녹지에 머무는 시간이 30분 늘 때마다 마음 건강이 나쁘다고 답할 오즈비는 0.937, 몸 건강이 나쁘다고 답할 오즈비는 0.918이었습니다[6]. 산책로와 운동 공간처럼 건강에 도움이 되는 시설을 갖춘 곳일수록 이 값이 낮게 나타났어요(마음 건강 오즈비 0.886)[6].

세계보건기구는 어르신께 일주일에 중간 강도 유산소 활동을 150~300분 이상 권하면서도, 권고량을 채우지 못해도 조금이라도 하는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다고 말합니다[7]. 그러니 처음부터 긴 산책을 말씀드릴 필요는 없어요.

## 어떤 공원이 부모님께 맞을까요?

가까운 거리와 함께 깨끗한지, 보기 좋은지도 살펴보면 좋습니다. 폴란드 조사에서 스트레스가 낮은 사람들은 여가 시간에 주로 걷기로 녹지를 더 오래 이용했고, 스트레스가 높을수록 녹지의 청결과 아름다움에 대한 만족이 낮았어요[3].

어르신의 눈으로 보는 일도 중요합니다. 한 소규모 연구에서는 65세 이상 8명이 동네를 다니며 사진과 음성 기록 83개를 남겼고, 공원과 보행로, 교통 안전을 고쳐 달라고 지역에 직접 제안했습니다[2]. 자녀 눈에는 평평해 보이는 길도 부모님께는 턱이 높고 쉴 곳이 없는 길일 수 있어요.

## 자주 묻는 질문

**Q. 공원 산책은 매일 해야 효과가 있나요?**
일주일에 몇 번이 가장 좋은지는 연구로는 아직 알 수 없어요. 조금이라도 움직이는 것이 안 하는 것보다 낫다는 권고를 기억해 두시면 충분합니다[7].

**Q. 집 근처에 공원이 없으면 어떻게 하나요?**
15분이 넘는다고 소용없다는 뜻은 아니에요. 영국 연구에서는 강이나 호수 같은 민물이 동네에 있는 사람들도 마음 건강이 좋다고 답했으니[4], 나무가 있는 길이나 냇가 산책로를 찾아보셔도 좋습니다.

**Q. 기분이 많이 가라앉으신 것 같은데 산책이면 될까요?**
이 연구들은 산책이 우울을 낫게 하는지를 시험한 것이 아니라 관련을 살핀 것입니다. 걱정이 크시면 산책과 별개로 의사와 상담해 보시길 권합니다.

## 오늘 해 볼 작은 걸음

- 부모님 댁에서 가장 가까운 공원까지 걸어서 몇 분인지 다음 방문 때 같이 재어 보세요.
- 가는 길에 쉬어 앉을 의자가 있는지, 턱이나 찻길이 위험하지 않은지 살펴보세요.
- 잔소리 대신 「이번 주말에 공원 같이 걷자」 한마디를 건네 보세요.

공원 산책 효과는 먼 곳에 있지 않습니다. 부모님 평소의 걸음이 닿는 가장 가까운 나무 아래에서 시작하면 됩니다.

sources.title: Exploring the role of exposure to green and blue spaces in preventing anxiety and depression among young people aged 14-24 years living in urban settings: A systematic review and conceptual framework.
sources.text: Despite the growing problem of anxiety and depression amongst young people aged 14-24 years living in urban settings, reviews about the role of exposure to green and blue spaces or nature in preventing anxiety and depression tend to focus on children, adults or sometimes adolescents. This review aims to explore whether exposure to green and blue spaces reduces the risk of anxiety and depression among young people aged 14-24 years living in urban settings and provide a conceptual framework. The academic databases CINAHL plus, Global Health, MEDLINE, ProQuest: Dissertations and Theses, PsycINFO, Scopus and OpenGrey were searched for research published in English between January 2000 and June 2020. All study designs were eligible. All included studies were assessed for quality. Searches identified 9208 sources with 48 meeting the inclusion criteria for the review. Experimental studies provided evidence that walking or being in a green space improves mood and state anxiety immediately following the intervention. Non-randomised evaluations and observational studies suggest that social interaction, physical activity, and mindfulness mediate the relationship between exposure to green space and mental health. We propose that the absence of noise and restorative qualities of green spaces promotes mindfulness and interrupt rumination, which in turn reduce the risk of anxiety disorders and depression. This review and the resulting conceptual framework provide evidence to healthcare professionals about the value of contact with nature and green social prescribing. For policymakers, it provides evidence about the value of bringing the benefits of forests, vegetation and nature into cities, and ensuring that these spaces are accessible and safe for young people to use.

sources.title: Older Adults Using Our Voice Citizen Science to Create Change in Their Neighborhood Environment.
sources.journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
sources.text: Physical activity, primarily comprised of walking in older adults, confers benefits for psychological health and mental well-being, functional status outcomes and social outcomes. In many communities, however, access to physical activity opportunities are limited, especially for older adults. This exploratory study engaged a small sample (N = 8) of adults aged 65 or older as citizen scientists to assess and then work to improve their communities. Using a uniquely designed mobile application (the Stanford Healthy Neighborhood Discovery Tool), participants recorded a total of 83 geocoded photos and audio narratives of physical environment features that served to help or hinder physical activity in and around their community center. In a facilitated process the citizen scientists then discussed, coded and synthesized their data. The citizen scientists then leveraged their findings to advocate with local decision-makers for specific community improvements to promote physical activity. These changes focused on: parks/playgrounds, footpaths, and traffic related safety/parking. Project results suggest that the Our Voice approach can be an effective strategy for the global goals of advancing rights and increasing self-determination among older adults.

sources.title: Green space attributes and their impact on perceived stress in Poland.
sources.text: Inconsistent findings and limited research from various countries highlight the need for further investigation of the relationship between Satisfaction with Green Space Attributes (SGSA) and Perceived Stress (PS) levels, which is crucial for informing urban planning strategists to improve residents' mental health using green areas. Presented study explored these relationships and differences in greenery usage and preferences in connection with self-perceived stress levels in the study area of post-socialist cities and other settlements units in Poland-the country belonging to the former block of Socialist Countries of People's Democracy (specific type of urbanism and influence on mentality of residents). Data collected in 2022 via Computer-Assisted Web Interviewing (CAWI) covered demographics, green space utilization, SGSA, and PS levels using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10). Statistical analyses, including Kruskal-Wallis rank ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U-test and multiple regression, revealed that lower PS levels were correlated with higher SGSA across various greenery elements. Individuals with low stress levels spent more time in green spaces for leisure activities, mainly walking. However, satisfaction with greenery decreased with increasing stress levels, especially regarding the decrease of cleanliness, aesthetics and greenery amount. Multiple regression identified significant predictors of stress levels, such as health, greenery aesthetics satisfaction, income, and green area accessibility for children. The study underscores the importance of well-designed, diversified green infrastructure to enhance residents' mental well-being. Accessible, well-maintained green spaces creating a network within urban environments are crucial for stress reduction. It is a guideline for policymakers and urban planners to create continuous green infrastructure consisting of various size and character green areas/elements and this green network should be as dense as possible, occupying every possible place.

sources.title: Neighbourhood blue space, health and wellbeing: The mediating role of different types of physical activity.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Evidence suggests that living near blue spaces such as the coast, lakes and rivers may be good for health and wellbeing. Although greater levels of physical activity (PA) may be a potential mechanism, we know little about the types of PA that might account for this. OBJECTIVES: To explore the mediating role of: a) 'watersports' (e.g. sailing/canoeing); b) 'on-land outdoor PA' in natural/mixed settings (e.g. walking/running/cycling); and, c) 'indoor/other PA' (e.g. gym/squash) in the relationships between residential blue space availability and health outcomes. METHODS: Using data from the Health Survey for England (n = 21,097), we constructed a path model to explore whether weekly volumes of each PA type mediate any of the relationships between residential blue space availability (coastal proximity and presence of freshwater) and self-reported general and mental health, controlling for green space density and a range of socio-economic factors at the individual- and area-level. RESULTS: Supporting predictions, living nearer the coast was associated with better self-reported general and mental health and this was partially mediated by on-land outdoor PA (primarily walking). Watersports were more common among those living within 5kms of the coast, but did not mediate associations between coastal proximity and health. Presence of freshwater in the neighbourhood was associated with better mental health, but this effect was not mediated by PA. CONCLUSIONS: Although nearby blue spaces offer potentially easier access to watersports, relatively few individuals in England engage in them and thus they do not account for positive population health associations. Rather, the benefits to health from coastal living seem, at least in part, due to participation in land-based outdoor activities (especially walking). Further research is needed to explore the mechanisms behind the relationship between freshwater presence and mental health.

sources.title: Proximity to public green spaces and depressive symptoms among South African residents: a population-based study.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Exposure to green spaces has been suggested to improve mental health and may reduce the risk of depression. However, there is generally limited evidence on the association between green spaces and depression originating from low-and middle-income countries and Africa in particular. Here, we investigate the association between proximity to public green spaces and depressive symptoms among residents of Gauteng Province, South Africa. METHODS: We used data from the 2017/2018 Gauteng quality of life survey. We included all individuals aged 18 years or older residing in the nine municipalities of Gauteng Province that completed the survey (n = 24,341). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-2. Proximity to public green spaces was defined as self-reported walking time (either less or greater than 15 min) from individuals' homes to the nearest public green space. To assess the association between access to public green spaces and depressive symptoms, we used mixed-effects models, adjusted for age, sex, population group (African, Indian/Asian, Coloured (mixed race), and White), educational attainment, and municipality. We additionally performed stratified analyses by age, sex, educational attainment, and population group to evaluate whether associations differed within subgroups. Associations are expressed as prevalence ratios (PR) and their 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). RESULTS: We observed a 6% (PR = 0.94, 95%CI = 0.92-0.96) prevalence reduction in depressive symptoms for individuals who reported that the nearest public green space was less than 15 min from their homes as compared to those who reported > 15 min. After stratification, this inverse association was stronger among females, individuals aged 35-59 years,those with higher levels of educational attainment, and Coloured individuals as compared to their counterparts. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that public green spaces close to residential homes may be associated with a reduction in the occurrence of depressive symptoms among urban populations in resource-constrained settings like South Africa.

sources.title: Weekly green space visit duration is positively associated with favorable health outcomes in people with hypertension: Evidence from Shenzhen, China.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: Studies from high income 'western' countries indicate that green space visit duration is associated with better health. However, scant comparable research has been done in developing countries with rapid urbanization and on the potential health impacts of specific green infrastructure. OBJECTIVE: Associations between green space visit duration, green infrastructure and various health outcomes were assessed in hypertensive patients. METHODS: A stratified multi-stage cluster random sampling method was applied to select 1116 patients with hypertension aged 35 years or older in Shenzhen, China. Face-to-face survey, physical examination and laboratory biochemical tests were applied to obtain information. Binary logistic regressions with restricted cubic splines were used to explore the degree of linearity in associations between green space visit duration and the following health outcomes: central obesity; diabetes; blood pressure; dyslipidemia; poor physical health; poor mental health. Models were adjusted for age, sex, education, marital status, occupation, and socioeconomic status. Further analysis was made for presence of the following health promoting green infrastructure: health knowledge promotion areas; walking trails; fitness areas; group exercise venues. RESULTS: Each additional 30 min green space visitation was linearly associated with lower odds of self-reported poor mental health [OR (95%CI): 0.937 (0.891-0.985)], self-reported poor physical health [OR (95%CI): 0.918 (0.872-0.966)], and central obesity [OR (95%CI): 0.951 (0.907-0.997)]. Odds of poor mental health [OR (95%CI): 0.886 (0.788-0.997)], poor physical health [OR (95%CI): 0.882 (0.782-0.996)] and central obesity [OR (95%CI): 0.855 (0.765-0.955)] were founded to decrease with a greater number of health promoting green infrastructure. CONCLUSION: More time spent in green space and with more types of green infrastructure were favourably associated with central obesity, and physical and mental health in people with hypertension.

sources.text: 65세 이상 어르신 권고: 일주일에 중간 강도 유산소 신체활동 150~300분 이상, 또는 고강도 75~150분 이상. 중간 강도 이상의 근력 운동을 일주일에 2일 이상. 기능적 균형과 근력을 강조한 복합 신체활동을 일주일에 3일 이상(기능을 높이고 낙상을 막기 위해). 앉아 있는 시간을 줄이고 어떤 강도든 신체활동으로 바꾸는 것이 건강에 이롭다. 권고량을 채우지 못하더라도 조금이라도 하는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다.
